guard: a teardown may only signal a pid whose creation identity it can prove (#969): a reused pid, a legacy live record, and a torn pin are refused and preserved; only an ESRCH-proven death clears a record
why: TWO INDEPENDENT HALVES OF ONE RULE. M1 breaks the shared verdict (the mismatch comparison in
verifyIdentityPin) and must redden the DELIVERY cell A1, whose sent===0 signal count is the
direct measurement of the pre-fix defect. M2 deletes the gate at the delivery call site
entirely and must redden E1, the legacy-record acceptance: the refusal is not only about
mismatched pins but about UNPROVABLE identity generally. Either mutation alone re-opens a
different half of #969, so both are load-bearing.
M1 IS THE ONE COMPARISON THE DESIGN TURNS ON, in the workspace seam all four teardown paths
share (stopManager, stopDelivery, stopAuthService, and down's stopLocalProcess for the broker
and web). Folding it to match makes every pinned record pass verification, which is precisely
the bare-pid behaviour the issue forbids. B1/B3/B5 redden too, but A1 is named because its
signal count is the exact shape the live repro killed a foreign process through.
M2 RESTORES THE PRE-FIX CALL SITE VERBATIM (no gate at all) at one real path, proving the
delivery teardown actually routes through the seam rather than the cells merely depending on
the shared module in some other way.
BOTH RUN THE CLI-LIB-BACKED SUITE, so they build first (implementations/cli resolves to dist/)
and rebuild in afterRestore - git cannot recover a gitignored dist compiled from the mutant.

mutations.name: M1 the shared verdict stops reporting mismatch (verifyIdentityPin folded to match)
mutations.find: return live === record.token ? { kind: "match" } : { kind: "mismatch", liveToken: live };
mutations.expectRed: A1 a REUSED pid (pin mismatch) is REFUSED by stopDelivery, never signalled
mutations.cell: A1 a REUSED pid (pin mismatch) is REFUSED by stopDelivery, never signalled
mutations.note: The one comparison the whole design turns on. Folding it to match makes every pinned record pass verification, which is precisely the bare-pid behaviour the issue forbids; A1's sent===0 count goes red the moment the signal is sent.

mutations.name: M2 identity gate deleted at the delivery call site (the pre-fix shape verbatim)
mutations.replace: void verifyIdentityPin; void identityRefusal; void identityUncertaintyRefusal;
mutations.expectRed: A1 a REUSED pid (pin mismatch) is REFUSED by stopDelivery, never signalled
mutations.cell: E1 a LEGACY (unpinned) live record is refused loud, never signalled
mutations.note: Removes the gate entirely at one real call site: the pre-fix shape verbatim. The suite is fail-fast, so the FIRST cell on that path reddens: A1 (the mismatch record is signalled, sent goes 1). E1's legacy refusal sits behind A1 on the same path and would redden in a non-fail-fast run; A1 is the named kill, and M2's distinct value over M1 is proving the CALL SITE routes through the seam, not the shared verdict alone.
